name: Unakoti Heritage Site (Rock Carvings)
description: Ancient open-air gallery of colossal rock-cut sculptures and bas-reliefs of Hindu deities, primarily Shaivite, carved into the hillsides of Unakoti. Centerpiece is the ~30-foot Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava (Shiva head). Dates to 7th-9th century CE; UNESCO Tentative World Heritage Site since 2022. Also known as Subrai Khung.
facts: Name means 'one less than a crore' from local legend of 99,99,999 carvings
About 8 km east of Kailashahar, 178 km from Agartala
Annual Ashokastami Mela attracts thousands of pilgrims
ASI protected site with streams and forested setting

name: Jampui Hills
description: Highest hill range in Tripura (~3,000 ft), known as the Eternal Hills of Spring or Orchid Paradise of India. Features lush greenery, orange orchards, misty landscapes, and panoramic views toward Mizoram and Bangladesh.
facts: Average elevation around 1,000 m; highest peak Betlingchhip at 930 m.
About 200-220 km from Agartala; nearest railhead Dharmanagar (~70 km).
Home to over 50 orchid species including rare Vanda coerulea.
Eden Tourist Lodge and local paying guest stays in Vanghmun.

name: Betlingchhip Peak
description: Highest point in Tripura at 930 m (also called Thaidawr or Betalongchhip), located on the Jampui ridge. Offers sunrise views of stacked ridges toward Mizoram hills and Bangladesh plains.
facts: Elevation 930 m, highest in the state.
Short walk or scramble from the road near Vanghmun.
Best at sunrise before mist fills the valleys.
Part of Jampui Hills range bordering Mizoram.

name: Vanghmun Village
description: Cleanest village in Tripura, perched on the Jampui ridge. Features neat Mizo homes, orange orchards, church, and access to viewpoints and homestays for authentic hill culture.
facts: Headquarters of Jampui Hills block; police station present.
Known for community cleanliness efforts.
Eden Tourist Lodge and local paying guests available.
About 220 km from Agartala, 55 km from Aizawl.

name: Rowa Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Compact wildlife sanctuary near Panisagar (about 86 hectares), rich in birds, primates, reptiles, and mixed forests. Ideal for short eco-trails, birdwatching, and peaceful nature visits.
facts: Established 1988; only sanctuary in northern Tripura.
About 18 km from Dharmanagar, 4-5 km from Panisagar.
Home to over 60 bird species, langurs, deer, and reptiles.
No permit required; accessible trails.

name: Shilchhara Buddha Waterfall
description: Hidden gem waterfall near Pecharthal, cascading amid lush forest with a Buddha statue beside the falls. Offers serene walks, meditation spots, and quiet immersion in nature.
facts: Located near Pecharthal in North Tripura.
Features a Buddha idol by the falls for peaceful ambiance.
Accessible via forest trails; best in non-monsoon for safety.
Lesser-known alternative to more crowded sites.

name: Kalibari Temple (Dharmanagar)
description: Prominent Kali temple in Dharmanagar town, serving as a spiritual and cultural center for local devotees. Active during festivals like Kali Puja with community gatherings.
facts: Located in Dharmanagar, headquarters of North Tripura.
Focal point for religious festivals and local culture.
Simple traditional architecture in a serene setting.
Accessible within the town.

name: Dharmanagar
description: Headquarters and largest town of North Tripura district, near the Bangladesh border. Gateway to Jampui Hills, Rowa Sanctuary, and other northern attractions, with markets and rail connectivity.
facts: Administrative center of North Tripura.
Nearest major railhead for Jampui Hills (~70 km).
Juri River flows through the town.
About 180-200 km from Agartala.

name: Dumboor Lake
description: Largest water body in Tripura covering about 41 sq km in Gandacherra subdivision of Dhalai district. Formed at the confluence of Raima and Sarma rivers, it features 48 islands, migratory birds in winter, and boating facilities. Named after the dumboor (damru) drum of Lord Shiva due to its shape.
facts: Area approximately 41 square kilometres with 48 islands
About 120 km from Agartala via Amarpur
Winter migratory birds and water sports available
Official listing under Dhalai district on NIC site
Near Tirthamukh where Gomati River originates

name: Narkel Kunja (Coconut Island)
description: Developed island resort and picnic spot on one of the 48 islands in Dumboor Lake, filled with coconut palms. Accessible by boat from the shore near Gandacherra, offering serene stays and views of the lake and surrounding hills.
facts: One of 48 islands in Dumboor Lake
Developed with tourist cottages and facilities
Name means coconut grove in Bengali
Boat access required from mainland jetty

name: Longtharai Mandir
description: Popular Shiva temple in the Longtharai hill range of Dhalai district. Longtharai is the Kokborok name for Lord Shiva; legend says he rested here on return from Kailash. Set amid scenic hills and forests, a major local pilgrimage spot.
facts: Located in Longtharai Valley area of Dhalai
About 102 km from Agartala
Hill means deep valley in local dialect
Surrounded by natural beauty ideal for visits

name: Kamaleswari Mandir
description: Prominent Kali temple in the center of Kamalpur town, Dhalai district. Kamaleswari is another name for Goddess Kali; the town is named after the temple. A major pilgrimage and cultural center about 35 km from Ambassa.
facts: Located in Kamalpur Nagar Panchayat
About 35 km from Ambassa HQ, 122 km from Agartala
Town named after the temple
Active during festivals like Kali Puja

name: Saika Waterfall (Tuisoi / Sulma Dongur Tuisoi)
description: Hidden gem waterfall in the Longtharai Reserve Forest near Saikar Bazar, Kamalpur subdivision. Also known as Tuisoi or Sulma Dongur Tuisoi, it cascades through dense forest with clear waters; recently developed with steps for access. One of the cleaner natural sites in Dhalai.
facts: Near Saikar Bazar on Kamalpur-Kumarghat road
In Longtarai Reserve Forest
Height around 150 feet in places; trek required
Also called Sulma Dongur Tuisoi Waterfall

name: Ambassa
description: Headquarters and main town of Dhalai district, serving as the administrative and transport hub. Gateway to Longtharai, Kamalpur, and northern attractions, with rail connectivity and markets amid forested hills.
facts: District headquarters of Dhalai
Ambassa railway station on the line
About 90-100 km from Agartala
Base for exploring Dhalai tourism sites

name: Tirthamukh
description: Sacred confluence site near Dumboor Lake where the Gomati River originates from the hydel project outlet. Site of the annual Poush Sankranti Mela on 14 January, attracting pilgrims for holy dips and cultural events. Blend of spiritual and natural significance.
facts: Origin point of Gomati River from Dumboor
Annual Poush Sankranti Mela on 14 January
Near the hydel project at the lake
Listed in association with Dumboor on Dhalai official site

name: Kamalpur
description: Largest sub-divisional town in Dhalai district, on the banks of the Dhalai River between Atharamura and Longtharai ranges. Named after Kamaleswari Temple, it serves as a base for northern Dhalai sites including the waterfall and border areas.
facts: Largest sub-divisional town in Dhalai
About 93 km from Agartala
Shares international border with Bangladesh
Home to Kamaleswari Mandir
